thread:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — elevated 5xx + client timeouts observed at gateway (region: us-west-2). paging oncall. escalation level: P1 :rotating_light:

sam (oncall): Ack. I'm on it. seeing alert in grafana too — error rate spike started ~10:12 UTC.

mike (sre): Sam, any signs from scheduler/batcher metrics? queue length, pending batches?

sam (oncall): Quick checks:
```
# query backlog
curl -s 'https://internal-metrics.local/api/query?metric=batcher.pending_batches&period=5m' | jq .
# result: pending_batches: 850 -> 1200 within 10m
```
Looks like pending batches increasing, avg batch wait ~2200ms, tail latency > 5s.

jia (prod): Customers are seeing gateway 502/504s. Support ticket volume rising. Product impact visible on top-line traffic graphs.

mike (sre): Head-of-line blocking pattern: single long-running KV cache miss / large context requests causing batcher saturation. Can you dump the top batch durations?

sam (oncall): Pulling from runtime tracer...
```
# top slow batches
curl -s 'https://tracer.local/top_batches?since=15m' | head -n 20
# sample:
# batch_id: b-9a8c, duration_ms: 18234, requests: 1, model: gpt-medium-q4
# batch_id: b-7c2f, duration_ms: 15789, requests: 1, model: gpt-medium-q4
# many single-request long batches
```
This screams long single-request batches preventing coalescing.

jia (prod): Do we have a recent deploy or config change? any rollout that adjusted batcher timeouts?

mike (sre): No deploy in last 30m per deploy-bot. Suspect workload skew: a small subset of clients sending very long sequences or using a legacy client doing sync calls.

sam (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce max_batch_wait to 50ms; 2) enable emergency eviction for single-request batches > 5s; 3) route a portion of traffic to degraded capacity (fallback model variant) to relieve scheduler. I'll apply 1 & 2 now.

sam (oncall): Applying config change to batcher pool 'us-west-2-a':
```
# prodctl rollout config
prodctl update batcher --pool us-west-2-a --set max_batch_wait_ms=50 --set single_request_eviction_threshold_ms=5000 --dry-run=false
```
sam (oncall): Done. Watching metrics.

mike (sre): Observability: prefix cache hit rate dropped 30% at spike start. means many cold contexts. eviction + lower wait should reduce HOL.

(1m later)
sam (oncall): Metrics trending: pending_batches -> 400, avg batch wait -> 180ms, 5xx rate down from 6.1% -> 1.8% so far.

jia (prod): Customer-impact quick calc: total ingress 120k req/min, error uplift estimated ~5k req/min at peak. CS queue: 12 open high-priority tickets (some on enterprise accounts).

cs-bot: Notifying CS leads for affected enterprise customers: acct-phi-tech, acct-ventra.

jia (prod): Notify both with initial message. no ETA yet, will update when stabilized <0.5% errors.

mike (sre): Also setting temporary traffic-shed rule for noisy client IP ranges to protect platform: adding 429 throttle for top offenders.

sam (oncall): Implemented 429 throttle for client-ids [cli-4432, cli-8899] (10% of their traffic random-shed). Reports expected in 30s.

(3m later)
sam (oncall): 5xx down to 0.9%, timeouts trending down. batcher backlog continues to clear. Rack-level GPU CPU < 60%.

jia (prod): Good. CS confirmed two enterprise customers seeing degraded responses; alerted their account teams.

mike (sre): Root cause hypothesis: a small number of clients submitted unusually long sequences with heavy KV cache misses which created single-request batches that ran long and blocked coalescing. Without eviction or lower max wait, batches held jobs waiting for more requests -> HOL.

sam (oncall): Next steps (short):
- keep eviction + reduced max_batch_wait for 30m and monitor
- schedule full rollout of eviction policies to other regions if stable
- follow-up postmortem to capture detection rule + auto-evict criteria
- contact infra to add fine-grained per-client rate limits for extreme long-sequence workloads

alisha (oncall-next): I'm taking over monitoring for the cooldown period. Sam, can you hand off any open runbook steps?

sam (oncall): Handing off: active mitigations in place, doubling sampling on slow-batches channel, CS notified. open items: verify tracer sampling, short-term throttle list, and prepare a k-v cache warmup plan.

alisha (oncall-next): Ack. I'll keep the channel updated. if error rate creeps above 2% we re-escalate.

jia (prod): I'll draft initial status for status.redwood.com: "Partial degradation in us-west-2 affecting some customers; mitigation applied; error rates decreasing." Will post in 10m unless numbers improve faster.

mike (sre): For the postmortem let's include: telemetry gap (slower detection of slow single-request batches), lack of per-client long-seq circuit breaker, and missing automatic eviction policy.

sam (oncall): Agreed. thanks all. closing the live mitigation loop; leaving channel open for follow-up. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigations applied, impact reduced. reopen if symptoms return.

alisha (oncall-next): final note: I'll keep monitoring overnight and create a follow-up ticket to standardize emergency batcher params. assigning to @mike for remediation work.

cs-bot: CS notes attached to incident-1779991234: customers contacted, two elevated tickets created, follow-up call scheduled with acct-phi-tech for 18:00 UTC.

sam (oncall): signing off handoff to Alisha at 11:18 UTC. leaving details in #incidents-postmortem-prep.

alisha (oncall-next): thanks. marking high-level timeline and action items for PM/IR.

(End of thread)
